A.lives: faint: a form earlier hands began and later hands carried on

B.lives: a courtyard is shared ground, with lanterns lit for every passer-by

C.lives: glass you can see through, and a shared hearth everyone gathers round

E.lives: stone foundations others laid, and glass you can see through

G.lives: clear as glass, a watch kept so the work can be inspected

H.lives: a lamp left lit for whoever comes after, to build by

J.lives: many voices sung together, each credited, the whole open to hearing

K.lives: faint: a dance handed down from teacher to dancer

L.lives: specimens labeled with their collectors, kept open for anyone to study

N.lives: a circle where everyone holds hands and learns the steps from those before

O.lives: faint: a light over a picture, for pictures the library may show freely

note: A Herbarium of Nights comes first because its specimens carry their collectors' names and stay open for anyone to study and build on, while The Glass Hearth is a warm second.
